sealed_candidate.answer: **Decision-support answer** (uses only the supplied fixture sources; no external evidence available or permitted here — the evidence pack is explicitly fictional, so this is a measurement-design recommendation, not a productivity verdict.)---### Q1: Which productivity outcome and comparison should drive the decision?**Outcome to use:** Evaluate agent-assisted delivery with matched tasks and measure quality-gate pass rate, human review time, rework, elapsed lead time, and total cost — and count failed or abandoned tasks. Do not infer causal benefit from accepted-PR counts. [measurement-policy]**Comparison to use:** Matched tasks, i.e., a control or matched baseline, not a raw monthly count.**Time horizon:** The policy does not specify a required horizon; the pilot covers one month, which is not established as sufficient. [measurement-context]**Accounting boundary:** Include reviewer hours, failed/abandoned work, and provider costs — the pilot note omits all of these. [measurement-policy] [measurement-context]---### Why the pilot's 40 accepted PRs cannot drive the decisionThe pilot reports 40 accepted pull requests in one month with **no task mix, no control group, no reviewer hours, no failure count, and no provider costs** [measurement-context]. Per the policy, accepted-PR counts must not be treated as causal evidence of productivity benefit [measurement-policy].---### Missing elements exposed (Obligation o1)- **Outcome:** defined by policy (quality, review time, rework, lead time, cost, failed work), but none of these are measured in the pilot. [measurement-policy] [measurement-context]- **Baseline/comparison:** absent — no control group or matched-task comparison exists in the supplied evidence. [measurement-context]- **Task mix:** absent. [measurement-context]- **Time horizon:** one month reported; adequacy undetermined by the policy. [measurement-context]**Status: unresolved.** The supplied sources define the required measurement framework but contain no baseline, task mix, or horizon data sufficient to close the decision.---### Limits (unresolved)- All sources are fictional fixture records; they establish policy, not empirical productivity.- The pilot's single-month, single-metric note cannot support a productivity or cost conclusion.- A blocking clarification remains: productive is undefined without a chosen outcome, baseline, task class, and time period (c1).**Recommendation:** Re-run the pilot with matched tasks, control group, full accounting of review hours, failures/rework, and provider costs before judging agent productivity. Do not make a go/no-go decision on accepted-PR counts.
